gold_assessment.reasoning: Gold: diarrhea as CC. Gen cc-001: chief complaint is diarrhea. Duration not in CC gold fact, so fully covered.
Gold: diarrhea for 3 days. Gen hpi-001: has had 3 days of diarrhea. Same content.
Gold: diarrhea associated with abdominal pain. Gen hpi-004: mild abdominal pain with diarrhea. Association is captured, with added severity qualifier.
Gold: no mucous or blood. Gen hpi-009 and hpi-010: denies blood and mucus in stool. Fully covered.
Gold: vomiting once. Gen hpi-005: one episode of vomiting. Same information.

Gold: still able to eat and drink. Gen hpi-008: maintaining oral fluid intake. Partial but adequate coverage of continued ability to take fluids; food not explicitly mentioned, but main concept (tolerating PO) appears also in asm-001. Considered covered.

Gold: watery diarrhea 4–5/day, sometimes mixed solid and loose. Gen hpi-002 and hpi-003: 4–5/day and stools watery to loose. Frequency and watery/loose are covered, but the specific detail about sometimes mixed solid and loose is omitted.
Gold: patient reports no fever. Gen hpi-007: possible low-grade fever, which conflicts. No generated fact captures explicit absence of fever.
Gold: loss of appetite. Gen hpi-006: decreased appetite. Same concept.

Gold: did not eat out prior to illness. Gen hpi-012: no suspect foods preceding illness. Related but not identical; “no suspect foods” is broader and does not explicitly state not eating out. Partially covered conceptually, but the specific 'did not eat out' detail is missing.
Gold: no recent foreign travel. Gen hpi-011: reports no recent travel. Covers absence of foreign travel and is slightly broader.
Gold: history of asthma. Gen pmh-001: history of asthma. Same.

Gold: yellow inhaler named Lapriso. Gen med-001/med-002: inhaler; reports “Lexapro” (yellow). Inhaler use and yellow color covered; the name differs (Lapriso vs Lexapro), so naming detail is not correctly captured.
Gold: no allergies. Gen allergy-001: no known drug allergies. Effectively equivalent in this context.
Gold: father died of bowel cancer 10 years ago. Gen fh-002: died of bowel CA at 62 (~10 yrs ago). Gold content is covered with extra detail (age).
Gold: family history of hypertension. Gen fh-001: father had HTN. This is a family history of hypertension.
Gold: no dehydration on exam. Gen pe-001: appears not dehydrated on video. Same clinical finding.
Gold: diagnosis is gastroenteritis. Gen asm-001 gives an assessment/summary of acute diarrhea likely self-limited, but does not explicitly state gastroenteritis as the diagnosis.

Gold: soft diet starting with crackers, soups, and mash. Gen plan-002: soft/simple foods like crackers, toast, jam, avoid certain foods; does not mention soups specifically but covers soft diet with crackers and similar items. Partially covers with some variation in examples.
Gold: drink plenty of fluids. Gen plan-001: encourage fluids/hydration. Same.
Gold: recommended Dioralyte. Gen plan-001: OTC oral rehydration salts such as Dioralyte. Same recommendation.

Gold: may progress diet to mashed vegetables after initial soft foods. Gen plan-003: after tolerating boiled veg/mash ~48h, then reintroduce meat/eggs/fish. The step of moving to mash/boiled veg is covered, but gen adds timing and reintroduction of proteins not in gold.
Gold: yogurts as probiotics to aid gut recovery. Gen plan-002: yogurt ok as probiotic. Matches.

Gold: if diarrhea >1 week or blood appears, stool sample will be required. Gen plan-004: if persistent or blood present, send stool sample; abx only if indicated. Stool sample triggers match; gen adds antibiotic management guidance not in gold.

Gold: if >8 episodes and dehydration risk, book appointment. Gen fu-001: if ≥6–8 stools/day, signs of dehydration, >1wk, or blood → contact clinic; significant dehydration → hospital. The >8 episodes with dehydration risk leading to appointment is conceptually covered, but thresholds and escalation details differ and are expanded.

gen_assessment.reasoning: Gold hpi-006: watery 4–5/day, sometimes mixed solid and loose. Gen: watery to loose stools. Supported for watery/loose character but omits the 'sometimes mixed solid and loose' nuance.
Gen: possible low-grade fever. Gold hpi-007: patient reports no fever. Direct conflict.
Gen: maintaining oral fluid intake. Gold hpi-005: still able to eat and drink. Consistent for fluids but gold explicitly includes food; thus partially supported (subset of oral intake).

Gen: no suspect foods preceding illness. Gold hpi-009: did not eat out. Overlapping concept (no obvious exposure) but not identical; gold specifically negates eating out, while gen refers broadly to suspect foods. Treated as partially supported.
Prior similar episodes after certain foods/travel are not mentioned anywhere in gold facts.
Gold facts do not mention whether meds were taken for current symptoms.
Gold med-001: yellow inhaler named Lapriso. Gen med-001: patient uses an inhaler (no name). Supported for inhaler use, but omits specific name and color.
Gen: medication referred to as "Lexapro" (yellow). Gold med-001: yellow inhaler named Lapriso. The names differ, so this directly contradicts the gold naming detail.
No gold fact addresses absence of vitals/physical exam documentation; this is new documentation-detail information.

Gen asm-001 summarizes acute diarrhea x3d, 4–5/day, no blood/mucus, mild abdo pain, 1 emesis, tolerating PO, likely self-limited. These elements are each supported by gold hpi-001–006 and hpi-003, hpi-005. However, gold explicitly diagnoses gastroenteritis (asm-001), which is not stated here, and 'likely self-limited' is an added clinical judgment. Thus largely supported description but incomplete vs gold diagnosis and with added interpretation.

Supported components: soft/simple foods including crackers (gold plan-001), yogurt as probiotic (gold plan-005). Added/modified components: toast, jam, specific avoidance of dairy/meat/eggs/fish during diarrhea are not in gold. Thus partially supported with additions.

Supported portion: progression to boiled vegetables/mash is consistent with gold plan-004. Added details: timing (~48h) and reintroduction of meat/eggs/fish are not present in gold. So partially supported with additions.

Gold fu-001: if diarrhea >1 week or blood appears, a stool sample is needed. Gen: if persistent or blood present, send stool sample; treat with antibiotics only if indicated. Stool-sample trigger is supported, but antibiotic management is an added element not in gold.

Gold fu-001 and fu-002: contact if diarrhea >1 week, blood in stool, and >8 episodes with dehydration risk. Gen fu-001: contact clinic if ≥6–8 stools/day, signs of dehydration, persistent >1 wk, or blood; hospital if significant dehydration. Core triggers are supported but thresholds (6–8 vs >8), and the explicit hospital escalation are additions/variations.
